articles.title_original: Enabling Bulk High-Temperature Additive Friction Stir Deposition of Steels with Polycrystalline Cubic Boron Nitride-Based Tools
articles.title_en: Enabling Bulk High-Temperature Additive Friction Stir Deposition of Steels with PCBN-Based Tools
articles.excerpt_original: Forgings currently have long lead times, motivating technology developments that produce parts with forge-like properties and have shorter timelines. Solid-state processes such as additive friction stir deposition (AFSD) offer this potential; however, large-scale deposition of high-temperature materials remains limited by tool durability, thermal management, and process stability. In this study, new polycrystalline cubic boron nitride (PCBN) AFSD tools, integrated with a liquid-cooled tool holder, are developed and evaluated for bulk deposition of 316 L stainless steel. Tool geometry modifications, including increased puck diameter and a drafted feed exit orifice, enabled graphite-free deposition by mitigating feedstock swaging. A minimum deposition rate is identified that maintains stable material flow and avoids excessive actuator forces. Comparing the use of PCBN tools with different shank materials shows that tungsten carbide shanked tools have improved thermal management relative to tools with a nickel-based shank. This improved thermal regulation resulted in more stable deposition, reduced tool wear, and successful multi-layer builds. Additionally, the use of a fully enclosed inert gas environment reduces surface oxidation and interlayer oxide formation. Electron microscopy was used to reveal limited tool-related contamination in the deposition. The contamination observed was dispersed boron nitride particles rather than continuous interfacial layers of tool material as observed in other literature. These results demonstrate that PCBN tooling combined with active cooling can enable stable, bulk AFSD of high-temperature alloys.
articles.summary_en: This academic study investigates the use of polycrystalline cubic boron nitride (PCBN) additive friction stir deposition tools combined with liquid-cooled tool holders for bulk deposition of 316L stainless steel. Tool geometry modifications and tungsten carbide shanks successfully improved thermal management, reduced tool wear, and enabled stable multi-layer builds with minimal contamination. The findings demonstrate that advanced tooling and active cooling can overcome previous limitations in high-temperature solid-state metal deposition.

articles.title_original: Critical Ripples and Dirac Fermions in Crystalline Membranes
articles.title_en: Critical Ripples and Dirac Fermions in Crystalline Membranes
articles.excerpt_original: Crystalline membranes hosting Dirac fermions, with graphene as the paradigmatic example, combine two low-energy sectors with sharply different dynamics: nonrelativistic flexural phonons and relativistic-like Dirac quasiparticles. We develop the low-energy field theory of this coupled system at charge neutrality and determine how this dynamical mismatch controls the coupling between the two sectors. In the long-wavelength flat phase, rotational symmetry ties the renormalization of the leading local scalar strain--density coupling to the scale-dependent bending rigidity, causing its dimensionless strength to decrease logarithmically. At the same time, flexural modes become parametrically slower than the Dirac fermions, so the resulting fermionic feedback vanishes as a power law.The flat phase is therefore stable against this perturbation. The physics changes when elastic interactions or electronic softening destabilize the membrane at a finite wavelength, selecting a ripple pattern formed by modes at $\pm\mathbf{Q}$. For an isolated pair of ordering wavevectors, provided that commensurability-induced phase pinning is irrelevant, the transition is governed by the bosonic Wilson--Fisher fixed point, while the Dirac fermions remain spectators. A genuinely hybrid electronic--structural critical point arises instead when symmetry permits a mass-type Dirac bilinear to share the ripple's momentum and quantum numbers, including horizontal-reflection parity. The transition is then described by the chiral-XY Gross--Neveu--Yukawa universality class. Using the known one-loop critical exponents, we characterize this transition, determine the induced secondary elastic distortion, and show that the fermionic and bosonic velocities lock in the isotropic continuum limit.
articles.summary_en: This academic study investigates the theoretical coupling between nonrelativistic flexural phonons and relativistic-like Dirac quasiparticles in crystalline membranes such as graphene. The researchers develop a low-energy field theory to examine the stability of the flat phase and identify a genuinely hybrid electronic-structural critical point governed by the chiral-XY Gross-Neveu-Yukawa universality class. The findings characterize the critical exponents, secondary elastic distortions, and velocity locking of fermionic and bosonic components in the isotropic continuum limit.

articles.title_original: Toward a High-Energy Hybrid Supercapacitor Based on Nb2O5/Graphene and P3MT/Graphene Nanocomposites
articles.title_en: High-Energy Hybrid Supercapacitor Developed Using Nb2O5/Graphene and P3MT/Graphene Nanocomposites
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract The increasing demand for energy-storage devices with high energy and power densities has driven efforts to develop innovative electrode materials. In this study, we report a simple, one-pot hydrothermal synthesis of Nb2O5/graphene nanoplatelet (GNP) nanocomposites. These nanocomposites were characterized using FEG-SEM and HR-TEM, revealing uniform decoration of Nb2O5 nanoparticles on GNPs. By optimizing the weight ratio of Nb2O5 to GNPs, the composite with 5 wt % Nb2O5 achieved a remarkable capacity of 230 mAh g–1 and excellent capacity retention, outperforming pristine Nb2O5. Furthermore, we present, for the first time, a lithium-ion hybrid capacitor employing Nb2O5/GNP nanocomposites as the anode and poly(3-methylthiophene) (P3MT)/GNP nanocomposites as the cathode in a non-aqueous electrolyte. A comparative analysis using a coin cell with a Nb2O5/GNP anode and an activated carbon cathode demonstrated that both the Nb2O5/GNP and P3MT/GNP-based configurations exhibited superior capacitance and rate capability. This work highlights the potential of Nb2O5/GNP and P3MT/GNP nanocomposites for next-generation energy-storage devices.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a simple one-pot hydrothermal synthesis method to produce Nb2O5/graphene nanoplatelet nanocomposites, achieving a high capacity of 230 mAh g–1 with excellent retention. The study further demonstrated a lithium-ion hybrid capacitor utilizing these nanocomposites as the anode and poly(3-methylthiophene)/graphene nanocomposites as the cathode. These configurations exhibited superior capacitance and rate capability compared to conventional setups, highlighting their potential for next-generation energy storage devices.

articles.title_original: Large-area CVD Graphene for Photogating-Based Photodetection
articles.title_en: Large-Area CVD Graphene for Photogating-Based Photodetection
articles.excerpt_original: Our work explores large-area CVD graphene as a scalable platform for photodetectors. We show that substrate-induced photogating in graphene/SiO$_2$/Si structures enables a photoconductivity signal in mono-, bi-, and trilayer CVD graphene. The devices respond to illumination with photon energies above the Si band gap and do not respond to telecom frequency, suggesting the photoconductivity mechanism through the photogating. Large sample area and gate voltage-dependent resistivity measurements allow us to prove the dominant role of the photogating directly, demonstrating similarity of the capacitive recharging current and the photoresponse. The sensitivity is the highest (995 A/W) for the monolayer graphene. Increasing the number of graphene layers reduces the sensitivity due to screening and parallel conduction, but can improve detectivity by lowering the noise level. The sensitivity of CVD graphene device depends on fabrication route of photolitography: device with metal contacts fabricated before graphene transfer show higher photoresponce. Thus, our work demonstrate the potential of industrially relevant CVD graphene for sensitive photogating-based photodetectors.
articles.summary_en: This academic study investigates large-area chemical vapor deposition (CVD) graphene as a scalable platform for photodetectors utilizing substrate-induced photogating. The researchers demonstrate that monolayer, bilayer, and trilayer CVD graphene structures exhibit significant photoconductivity under illumination with photon energies above the silicon band gap. Results indicate that monolayer graphene achieves the highest sensitivity, while increasing the number of layers improves detectivity by reducing noise levels.

articles.title_original: Computational Insights into Polymer Binder–Graphene Interfaces: Chitosan-Functionalized Graphene Oxide as a Sustainable Platform for Lithium-Ion Batteries
articles.title_en: Computational Study of Polymer Binder and Graphene Interfaces for Sustainable Lithium-Ion Batteries

Structural, energetic, electronic, and topological features were analyzed using counterpoise-corrected interaction energies, frontier-orbital descriptors, molecular electrostatic potential maps, projected density of states, noncovalent interaction analysis, and quantum theory of atoms in molecules topology. Final interaction energies were obtained at the M06-2X/def2-TZVP level with Boys–Bernardi counterpoise correction to provide a more robust description of weak noncovalent adsorption. articles.summary_en: Researchers used density functional theory calculations to evaluate the interactions between binder monomers and pristine graphene or chitosan-functionalized graphene oxide. The study found that most binder-surface interactions operate within a weak, near-thermoneutral adsorption regime, providing fundamental insights into interface design for sustainable lithium-ion batteries. Surface functionalization increases chemical heterogeneity and local contact directionality without yielding strong global adsorption energies.

articles.title_original: Synthesis, Structural Characteristics, and Applications of Vertically Oriented Graphene: A Review
articles.title_en: Synthesis, Structural Characteristics, and Applications of Vertically Oriented Graphene: A Review
articles.excerpt_original: Vertically oriented graphene (VG), few-layer graphene nanosheets that stand upright on the substrate, has attracted significant attention within the carbon nanomaterial family owing to its unusual structural geometry and the resulting electrochemical and physical performance advantages. This review provides a comparative analysis of the two dominant synthesis routes: thermal chemical vapor deposition (Thermal CVD) and plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition (PECVD). The plasma sheath electric field is identified as the key mechanism responsible for deterministic vertical growth. The roles of principal process parameters (plasma power density, gas composition, chamber pressure, and substrate bias) in shaping nanosheet morphology and crystallinity are examined. Applications of VG in electrochemical energy storage, high-sensitivity sensing, cold-cathode field emission, and electrocatalysis are surveyed. Outstanding challenges, including large-area uniformity, low-temperature growth, and long-term stability, are discussed alongside emerging trajectories such as machine-learning-driven process optimization and engineered two-dimensional heterostructures. Together, these discussions yield a coherent structure–property–function picture of VG that underpins its push toward practical device deployment.
articles.summary_en: This review paper compares thermal CVD and plasma-enhanced CVD synthesis routes for vertically oriented graphene, focusing on the role of plasma sheath electric fields in deterministic growth. It examines key process parameters affecting nanosheet morphology and surveys applications in electrochemical energy storage, sensing, and electrocatalysis. Finally, it outlines current challenges such as large-area uniformity and low-temperature growth alongside emerging trends like machine-learning process optimization.

articles.title_original: Design and Optimization of High-G Graphene MEMS Acceleration Sensor
articles.title_en: Design and Optimization of High-G Graphene MEMS Acceleration Sensor
articles.excerpt_original: High-g accelerometers are in high demand across sectors such as aerospace, defense, and industrial inspection. This paper presents a MEMS accelerometer based on graphene piezoresistors, designed for precise acceleration measurement under sudden impacts, intense vibrations, and extreme conditions, such as engine fault diagnosis and weapon impact testing. A step-by-step structural optimization and simulation analysis were conducted using finite-element simulation. Taking the peak strain at the beam root, the first-order natural frequency, and the maximum equivalent stress as optimization objectives, progressive parametric optimization was sequentially performed on four progressive architectures: a simple beam, a beam mass, a beam mass with stress concentration grooves, and a beam mass with stress concentration grooves and symmetric masses. The results indicate that the introduction of a central mass enhances the peak strain by more than 15 times compared to the simple beam. The addition of stress concentration grooves further increases the strain by approximately 30%. Finally, the incorporation of symmetric masses yields a further 9% strain enhancement while reducing cross-axis sensitivity by 5.6%, effectively suppressing off-axis interference. The final structure achieves maximized strain while maintaining a first-order natural frequency above 200 kHz, with the maximum equivalent stress staying within the allowable limit. This optimal comprehensive performance provides essential technical support for high-performance graphene-based accelerometers. In addition to the mechanical structural optimization, the graphene piezoresistors were treated as surface sensing regions at the beam-root locations, and the area-averaged longitudinal strain was extracted as the input of a pi
articles.summary_en: This academic study presents the structural design and finite-element optimization of a high-g MEMS accelerometer utilizing graphene piezoresistors. Researchers evaluated progressive architectures including beam-mass layouts and stress concentration grooves to maximize strain and suppress cross-axis sensitivity while maintaining a high natural frequency. The optimized sensor configuration provides enhanced performance for extreme conditions such as aerospace impacts and engine diagnostics.

articles.title_original: MXene-enabled micro/nanofluidic transport interfaces: ordered nanochannels, hydration regulation, and responsive ion transport
articles.title_en: Review on MXene-Enabled Micro and Nanofluidic Transport Interfaces
articles.excerpt_original: MXenes have emerged as promising building blocks for micro/nanofluidic transport interfaces because of their lamellar architecture, hydrophilic surface terminations, solution processability, and high electrical conductivity. Unlike conventional porous membranes, stacked MXene nanosheets can form slit-like nanochannels that confine water and ions within angstrom-to nanometer-scale spaces. Recent advances show that ion transport in MXene channels is governed not only by interlayer spacing, but also by channel alignment, lateral flake size, defect density, surface terminations, hydration structure, and interlayer chemistry. Ordered nanochannels, biomimetic sub-nanochannels, and directionally functionalized channel entrances have enabled improved ion selectivity and permeability. Meanwhile, confined water and cation intercalation can regulate local transport barriers, swelling behavior, and nanochannel stability. Crosslinked networks, hydrogel pillars, and mixed-dimensional assemblies further improve the mechanical reliability of MXene channels under aqueous conditions. In addition, light-responsive, pH-gated, voltage-gated, and electroconductive MXene membranes highlight the potential of dynamic ion transport and flow-responsive interfaces. This mini review summarizes recent progress in MXene-enabled micro/nanofluidic transport interfaces, emphasizing structure–transport–stability–response relationships and future opportunities for MEMS-compatible and device-oriented fluidic systems.
articles.summary_en: This academic review explores recent advancements in MXene-based micro and nanofluidic transport interfaces, focusing on ordered nanochannels, hydration regulation, and responsive ion transport. The study highlights structure-transport-stability relationships in stacked MXene nanosheets and discusses their potential in MEMS-compatible fluidic systems.

articles.title_original: Microstructure and Properties of Surface Modification of Hexagonal Boron Nitride and Carbon Nanotubes/Magnesium Composites
articles.title_en: Microstructure and Properties of Surface Modification of Hexagonal Boron Nitride and Carbon Nanotubes/Magnesium Composites
articles.excerpt_original: In order to enhance the wettability and scattering between matrix and reinforcement, the effects of incorporating hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) into magnesium-carbon nanotubes (Mg-0.5 weight percent CNTs) nanocomposites were successfully investigated for the first time in this paper. On the produced sample&s;s tribological testing, microstructural analysis, hardness values were elucidated. Wear rate and hardness were all improved when the 2 weight percent of h-BN content was compared to Mg-0.5%wtCNTs-0%h-BN. articles.summary_en: This academic study investigates the integration of hexagonal boron nitride into magnesium-carbon nanotube nanocomposites using electroless chemical deposition and double stir casting techniques. articles.title_original: Deterministic Integration of Quantum Emitters and Optical Cavities in a Van Der Waals Crystal
articles.title_en: Deterministic Integration of Quantum Emitters and Optical Cavities in Hexagonal Boron Nitride
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT Single‐photon emitters in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) combine bright optical emission with optically addressable spin states, offering a promising platform for integrated quantum photonics. However, their stochastic creation and spectral variability have prevented deterministic integration with photonic cavities. Here we demonstrate a fabrication protocol that enables precise, deterministic coupling of pre‐selected visible emitters to circular Bragg grating (CBG) cavities in hBN. By patterning etched alignment markers and performing pre‐fabrication confocal mapping, we locate emitters with sub‐micron accuracy and design cavity geometries matched to their zero‐phonon line wavelengths. The resulting devices show enhanced emission and reliable spectral alignment between emitter and cavity mode. This work establishes a deterministic cavity‐emitter integration scheme in a van der Waals material and provides a scalable route toward on‐chip quantum photonic and spin‐based platforms using hBN.
articles.summary_en: This academic study demonstrates a novel fabrication protocol for the precise and deterministic coupling of pre-selected single-photon emitters to circular Bragg grating cavities in hexagonal boron nitride. By utilizing alignment markers and pre-fabrication confocal mapping, researchers achieved sub-micron accuracy in matching cavity geometries to emitter wavelengths. This advancement establishes a scalable route toward on-chip quantum photonic and spin-based platforms using van der Waals materials.

articles.title_original: Regulation of vacancy formation in h-BN via carbon doping toward improved resistive switching
articles.title_en: Carbon Doping Regulates Vacancy Formation and Resistive Switching in Hexagonal Boron Nitride
articles.excerpt_original: Hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) exhibits promising potential in resistive switching applications, yet the performance variability remains a major obstacle, primarily due to the uncontrollable nature of intrinsic defects. Carbon doping can offer a potential means to regulate defect types and their spatial distribution. However, the microscopic mechanisms by which carbon dopants regulate defects in h-BN remain unclear. In this work, the modulation of the resistive switching behavior in h-BN based RRAM by carbon dopants is studied using first-principles calculations. The results indicate that carbon substituted for boron (CB) not only promotes the formation of boron vacancies (VB), but its interaction with vacancies further facilitates vacancy clustering around the dopant. Notably, interlayer interactions depend on defect type, with in adjacent layers exhibiting mutual repulsion, whereas nitrogen vacancies (VN) attract and stabilize . Climbing image nudged elastic band (CI-NEB) calculations demonstrate that resistive switching does not rely on migration but is mediated by boron-nitrogen divacancy (VBN) enabled conductive bridge formation (-1q/-2q charge states) and breaking (0q/+1q charge states). Non-equilibrium Green's function (NEGF) transport calculations verify a pronounced enhancement of the current upon conductive bridge formation. This work provides fundamental theoretical insights for defect engineering in the development of h-BN based RRAM.
articles.summary_en: This academic study uses first-principles calculations to investigate how carbon doping regulates defect types and spatial distribution in hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) for resistive switching applications. The results show that carbon substitution promotes boron vacancy formation and facilitates vacancy clustering, while transport calculations verify enhanced current upon conductive bridge formation.

articles.title_original: Exciton–phonon coupling in two-dimensional materials: from phenomena to applications
articles.title_en: Exciton–Phonon Coupling in Two-Dimensional Materials: Fundamentals and Applications
articles.excerpt_original: Exciton–phonon coupling is a fundamental interaction governing the optical, electronic, and thermal properties of semiconductors. Two-dimensional (2D) materials, with reduced dielectric screening and strong confinement, exhibit enhanced exciton binding energies and exciton–phonon coupling, offering a rich platform for studying related phenomena. Here, we provide a brief review of exciton–phonon interactions in 2D materials. We first introduce the basic physical mechanisms, including the Huang–Rhys factor and different coupling regimes. Then, we summarize representative phenomena such as phonon-assisted upconversion, self-trapped excitons, exciton formation dynamics, and phonon-mediated dark-exciton processes. Next, we discuss exciton–spin–phonon coupling in van der Waals magnetic materials. Finally, we highlight emerging applications, including solid-state laser cooling, single-photon sources, and exciton-optomechanics, and provide perspectives on future research directions in this field.
articles.summary_en: This review paper examines exciton–phonon interactions in two-dimensional materials, highlighting enhanced binding energies and coupling strength resulting from reduced dielectric screening and quantum confinement. It covers fundamental physical mechanisms, representative phenomena such as phonon-assisted upconversion and dark-exciton processes, and discusses emerging technological applications including solid-state laser cooling and single-photon sources.

articles.title_original: Flexible AlGaN/GaN HEMT devices exfoliated from Si substrate by electrochemical etching
articles.title_en: Flexible AlGaN/GaN HEMT Devices Exfoliated from Silicon via Electrochemical Etching
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Flexible electronic/optoelectronic devices based on wide-bandgap materials are gaining great attention due to the demand of versatile commercial and military applications. This paper presents an electrochemical etching technique for high-quality transfer of AlGaN/GaN high-electron-mobility transistor (HEMT) thin films from silicon substrate to temporary substrates. Unlike conventional mechanical grinding, this method avoids mechanical damage to the device, thereby preserving the structural integrity and electrical properties of the heterostructure. The surface morphology of the exfoliated HEMT thin films was confirmed by atomic force microscopy images with a root mean square roughness of 1.9 nm. This transfer technique offers a wafer-scale and low-damage route for fabricating high-performance flexible III-nitride semiconductor devices for wearable, radio-frequency, and power applications.
articles.summary_en: This academic study details an electrochemical etching technique for transferring AlGaN/GaN high-electron-mobility transistor thin films from silicon to temporary substrates without mechanical damage. The method preserves structural integrity and electrical performance, yielding a surface roughness of 1.9 nm. This wafer-scale process enables the fabrication of high-performance flexible III-nitride semiconductor devices for wearable, radio-frequency, and power applications.

articles.title_original: Identifying Contact Barrier Types in Few-Layer MoS2 Devices Using Correlative IV, LBIC, and Bias-Dependent KPFM
articles.title_en: Correlative IV, LBIC, and Bias-Dependent KPFM Framework for Identifying Contact Barrier Types in Few-Layer MoS2 Devices
articles.excerpt_original: Electrical contacts between metals and two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors such as molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) critically govern device performance, yet their microscopic nature remains difficult to disentangle using any single characterization technique. Here we present an integrated experimental framework that combines current-voltage (IV) characterization, laser beam induced current (LBIC) mapping, and bias-dependent Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) to comprehensively resolve the contact properties of few-layer MoS2-based two-terminal devices under ambient conditions. IV measurements deliver macroscopic transport characteristics as a function of bias voltage and illumination conditions. LBIC maps the local photocurrent response with micrometer spatial resolution, revealing the position and nature of internal electric fields at MoS2-metal interfaces. KPFM, operated under an applied static bias rather than in the conventional work-function mode, provides nanoscale-resolved potential distributions that quantify the relative magnitudes and spatial locations of contact barriers. We apply this framework to three representative devices - one exhibiting ohmic-like and two exhibiting diode-like contact behavior - and demonstrate that the combined analysis can unambiguously identify whether the dominant barrier is of Schottky or tunnel type and determine the asymmetry between the two contacts. We further demonstrate that thermal annealing significantly reduces the total resistance, while contact barriers remain the dominant source of resistance. The methodology is directly transferable to other 2D semiconductor-metal systems and provides a practical yet comprehensive route toward a quantitative microscopic understanding of 2D device contacts.
articles.summary_en: Researchers present an integrated experimental framework combining current-voltage characterization, laser beam induced current mapping, and bias-dependent Kelvin probe force microscopy to resolve contact properties in few-layer MoS2 devices. The methodology successfully identifies Schottky versus tunnel barriers and analyzes asymmetry across different contact behaviors. Furthermore, the study demonstrates that thermal annealing reduces total resistance while contact barriers remain the dominant resistance source.

articles.title_original: Hybrid metal-semiconductor quantum dots in InAs as a platform for quantum simulation
articles.title_en: Hybrid Metal-Semiconductor Quantum Dots in InAs for Quantum Simulation
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Arrays of hybrid metal-semiconductor quantum dots offer a new approach to quantum simulation, with key advantages over arrays of conventional quantum dots. Because the metallic component of these hybrid dots has a quasi-continuous level spectrum, each site in an array can be effectively electronically identical; in contrast, each conventional semiconductor quantum dot has its own spectral fingerprint. Meanwhile, the semiconductor component retains gate-tunability of intersite coupling. This combination creates a scalable platform for simulating correlated ground states driven by Coulomb interactions. We report the fabrication and characterization of hybrid metal-semiconductor dots, featuring a submicron metal island transparently contacting a gate-confined region of an InAs quantum well with tunable couplings to macroscopic leads. Tuning the dot-lead coupling to the weak-coupling limit yields highly-uniform Coulomb peaks, with no resolvable excitation spectrum in the Coulomb diamonds. We propose a realistic device design for a hybrid dot-based linear array quantum simulator and outline the correlated many-body physics accessible in this architecture.
articles.summary_en: This academic study demonstrates the fabrication and characterization of hybrid metal-semiconductor quantum dots utilizing an InAs quantum well platform. The research highlights the advantages of combining a metallic component with a gate-tunable semiconductor region to achieve uniform Coulomb peaks for scalable quantum simulation. This architecture provides a robust foundation for investigating correlated many-body physics driven by Coulomb interactions.

articles.title_original: Inverse Piezoelectricityand Carrier-Mediated PhaseInstability as Intrinsic Limits in Two-Dimensional Transition MetalDichalcogenide-Based Devices
articles.title_en: Intrinsic Electrical Degradation Mechanisms in Two-Dimensional Transition Metal Dichalcogenide Devices
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract 2D transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) are layered semiconducting materials with significant electromechanical coupling, whereby electric fields induce mechanical deformation and mechanical strain alters electronic properties. This electromechanical coupling enables interesting device physics, but its role in electrical degradation remains unexplored. We establish a fundamental framework that decouples and isolates how electric field strength and carrier density independently drive degradation in monolayer MoS2 planar FETs, revealing two competing intrinsic mechanisms that are qualitatively distinct from and largely undetected in conventional bulk semiconductor reliability physics. In carrier-depleted channels (field-dominant regime), strong out-of-plane electric fields in the absence of carriers trigger a dominant inverse piezoelectric effect, inducing compressive strain that dramatically lowers the formation energy for sulfur vacancies. This creates a runaway process where defects accumulate and initiate failure near the drain. Conversely, in carrier-rich channels (carrier-dominant regime), mobile electrons stabilize the semiconducting 2H to metallic 1T phase transition in the presence of dominant tensile strain due to an in-plane electric field, forming highly conductive filaments that burn through via Joule heating. Electrical measurements combined with Raman spectroscopy, photoluminescence, and scanning capacitance microscopy reveal diagnostic signatures distinguishing these pathways. These findings indicate that electrical degradation in 2D materials is strongly governed by material-specific properties, namely, piezoelectricity and phase stability, which are largely absent in bulk semiconductors. articles.summary_en: Researchers have identified two competing intrinsic degradation mechanisms in monolayer MoS2 planar field-effect transistors: an inverse piezoelectric effect driven by strong electric fields in carrier-depleted channels, and carrier-mediated phase instability in carrier-rich channels leading to Joule heating failure. The study establishes a predictive framework for electrical degradation in 2D transition-metal dichalcogenides, highlighting unique material-specific phenomena absent in conventional bulk semiconductors.

articles.title_en: A Refined 2D Simulation Framework for Optimizing Superconducting Qubits Using Process-Realistic Geometry

articles.summary_en: This academic study proposes a data-driven framework combining computer vision and 2D energy participation ratio (EPR) simulations to optimize superconducting transmon qubits. By extracting realistic geometric parameters from SEM cross-sections, the researchers analyzed how interface thickness, substrate over-etch depth, and trench angle impact device decoherence. The findings identify substrate over-etch depth and trench angle as dominant drivers of performance, offering design guidelines for improved coherence times.

articles.title_original: Orbital Multiferroicity in Twist Monolayer–Bilayer Graphene
articles.title_en: Orbital Multiferroicity and Competitive Orders Observed in Twisted Monolayer-Bilayer Graphene
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Owing to their electrically tunable nature, orbital ferroic orders have attracted intense interests and possess great potential for applications in next-generation electronic devices. Systems hosting coexisting multiple orbital ferroic orders, namely, orbital multiferroicity, have emerged as promising platforms to probe the interplay between these orders, yet it remains largely unexplored. Herein, we report the orbital multiferroicity and the intriguing competitive behavior between different orbital ferroic orders in twisted monolayer–bilayer graphene (tMBG), which facilitates the attainment of multidimensional control. At three electrons per moiré unit cell, two distinct orbital ferroic orders, that is, orbital ferromagnetic and ferro-valleytronic orders, emerge and exhibit a competitive relation. Under low magnetic fields, the orbital ferromagnetic energy dominates the electronic free energy and results in hysteretic transitions triggered by magnetic field and carrier density. However, with increasing magnetic field, the orbital ferro-valleytronic energy becomes comparable to the orbital ferromagnetic energy, inducing additional transitions driven by magnetic fields and electrical displacement fields. Our findings highlight the potential of orbital multiferroicity for enabling multidimensional control in nonvolatile information storage devices.
articles.summary_en: Researchers report the observation of orbital multiferroicity and competitive orbital ferroic orders in twisted monolayer-bilayer graphene. The study demonstrates hysteretic transitions driven by magnetic fields, carrier density, and electrical displacement fields at three electrons per moiré unit cell. These findings highlight the potential of such systems for enabling multidimensional control in nonvolatile information storage devices.

articles.title_original: Synthesis and characterization of polycitric acid-functionalized MXene nanofluid for enhanced oil recovery
articles.title_en: Polycitric Acid-Functionalized MXene Nanofluid for Enhanced Oil Recovery
articles.excerpt_original: In this study, a polycitric acid-functionalized MXene (Ti 3 C 2 T x ) (F-MX) nanofluid was synthesized, characterized, and evaluated for enhanced oil recovery (EOR). MXene nanosheets were prepared via selective HF etching of the Ti 3 AlC 2 MAX phase and subsequently functionalized through in situ polymerization of citric acid, an environmentally friendly and naturally derived polymer. Characterization by Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), X-ray diffraction (XRD), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX), and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) confirmed successful exfoliation, interlayer expansion and surface functionalization of MXene nanosheets. The F-MX nanofluid exhibited excellent colloidal stability in both deionized water and brines containing up to 5–20 wt% NaCl for 3 months. Interfacial tension (IFT) measurements demonstrated reductions from 45.7 ± 0.27 mN/m in deionized (DI) water and 48.3 ± 0.25 mN/m in brine to 34.99 ± 0.28 mN/m and 38.96 ± 0.32 mN/m, respectively, at a concentration of 0.1 wt%. Micromodel flooding experiments showed a substantial improvement in oil recovery, from 21% with conventional brine injection to 59% with F-MX nanofluid injection. The results demonstrate that F-MX nanofluids significantly enhance oil recovery through combine effects of enhance colloidal stability, effective transport throu
articles.summary_en: This academic study reports the synthesis and characterization of a polycitric acid-functionalized MXene nanofluid evaluated for enhanced oil recovery (EOR) applications. The functionalized MXene nanosheets exhibited high colloidal stability in brines, reduced interfacial tension, and successfully modified rock wettability, resulting in substantially improved oil recovery in micromodel flooding experiments. The research highlights the potential of environmentally friendly functionalized 2D materials beyond graphene for energy-related subsurface applications.

articles.title_original: Defect-EngineeredHexagonal Boron Nitride EnablesIonic Conduction for Lithium Metal Batteries
articles.title_en: Defect-Engineered Hexagonal Boron Nitride Enables Ionic Conduction for Lithium Metal Batteries
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract The practical implementation of lithium metal anodes has been hindered by uncontrollable dendrite formation and interfacial instability. This study presents a defect engineering of multiplayer hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) that enhances ionic conductivity through argon ion irradiation. A cell-level demonstration was performed using commercially available, large-area CVD-grown h-BN films subjected to industrial-scale argon ion implantation. Direct evidence was provided by integration of these exfoliated flakes into a hybrid microfluidic-microelectronic chip, confirming that controlled vacancy defects transform h-BN into an efficient lithium-ion conductor while preserving its intrinsic electrical insulation. The results confirmed improved lithium–metal anode stability, achieving dendrite-free cycling with Li plating/stripping Coulombic efficiencies exceeding 99.5% for about 1000 cycles. Further assembly of irradiated h-BN in lithium–sulfur batteries effectively mitigates the polysulfide shuttle effect, sustaining over 97% specific capacity around 300 cycles. These results establish a robust, scalable interface engineering route for next-generation lithium metal batteries that combine high ionic transport with excellent electrical insulation.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a defect engineering method using argon ion irradiation on multi-layer hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) films to enhance ionic conductivity while maintaining electrical insulation. Integrated into lithium metal and lithium-sulfur batteries, the modified h-BN films enabled dendrite-free cycling, high Coulombic efficiencies, and mitigated the polysulfide shuttle effect. This scalable interface engineering approach offers improved performance and stability for next-generation energy storage systems.

articles.title_original: From Migration–HealingReconstruction to ChemicalSegregation: Atomistic Origins of High-Temperature Evolution in CubicBoron Nitride Nanoparticles Revealed by Machine Learning PotentialSimulations
articles.title_en: Atomistic Mechanisms of High-Temperature Evolution in Cubic Boron Nitride Nanoparticles
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Cubic boron nitride (c-BN) nanoparticles are promising for extreme-condition applications, yet their atomistic evolution remains poorly understood. Here, we develop a high-fidelity machine learning potential and perform large-scale deep potential molecular dynamics simulations to investigate their high-temperature behavior. A universal reconstruction pathway is revealed, involving defect formation, inward-to-outward atomic migration, and progressive healing into multilayer hexagonal BN (h-BN). This mechanism is validated across multiple morphologies and exposed facets and is found to be strongly dependent on facet and termination. Furthermore, temperature-programmed dynamics identify ∼1800 K as the critical threshold for activating large-scale atomic flux, driving the transformation from core–shell architectures to multishell fullerene-like h-BN structures. At extreme temperatures (&gt;3300 K), chemical segregation emerges, leading to the formation of boron clusters and polynitrogen chains, consistent with experimental observations. We further compared the reconstruction behaviors of isoelectronic nanodiamond and c-BN nanoparticles, revealing that c-BN exhibits superior thermal stability and enhanced self-healing capability, originating from the higher kinetic barriers associated with partially ionic B–N bonds relative to covalent C–C bonds.
articles.summary_en: Researchers used machine learning potential molecular dynamics simulations to investigate the high-temperature behavior and structural evolution of cubic boron nitride (c-BN) nanoparticles. The study reveals a universal reconstruction pathway leading to multilayer hexagonal BN structures and identifies critical temperature thresholds for phase transitions and chemical segregation. Comparisons with nanodiamonds highlight the superior thermal stability and self-healing capabilities of c-BN nanoparticles.

articles.title_original: Surface-modified h-BN suppresses thermal-oxidative degradation of synthetic ester oil-paper insulation through interfacial hydronium-ion regulation
articles.title_en: Surface-Modified h-BN Suppresses Thermal-Oxidative Degradation in Synthetic Ester Oil-Paper Insulation
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Thermal-oxidative aging of synthetic ester oil-paper insulation is closely associated with acid-catalyzed depolymerization of cellulose, in which hydronium ions play a key role at the oil-paper interface. In this work, KH550-modified hexagonal boron nitride (KH550-hBN) nanoparticles were introduced into a synthetic ester oil-paper insulation system to examine whether the nanoparticle interface can regulate the interaction and transport behavior of hydronium ions during aging. Accelerated thermal aging was carried out at 155 °C in air, and the evolution of acid value, dielectric loss, AC breakdown strength, tensile strength, and degree of polymerization (DP) was evaluated. Compared with the unmodified system, the nanomodified system showed lower dielectric loss and acid value, while the DP of the impregnated paper remained 13.5% higher after 672 h of aging. The results showed that KH550-hBN weakens the interaction between cellulose and hydronium ions, reduces hydrogen-bond formation between them, and suppresses hydronium-ion diffusion. Molecular dynamics simulations and accelerated aging tests reveal that the functionalized nanoparticle interface regulates hydronium-ion behavior, reducing acid-catalyzed cellulose degradation and improving dielectric and mechanical retention. The findings offer a mechanistic approach to enhancing the longevity of electrical insulation materials.

articles.title_original: A Unified Machine‐Learning Framework for Predicting Barrier‐Free Metal Contacts in 2D Semiconductor Transistors
articles.title_en: Unified Machine-Learning Framework for Predicting Barrier-Free Metal Contacts in 2D Semiconductor Transistors
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT Achieving low‐resistance, reproducible metal contacts remains a major obstacle to integrating two‐dimensional (2D) semiconductors into deeply scaled CMOS technologies. Despite intensive study of selected semiconductor‐metal (S‐M) interfaces, particularly those based on transition‐metal dichalcogenides, contact optimization continues to rely heavily on experimental, and computational trial‐and‐error, in part due to variations in interface structure and processing that obscure intrinsic trends and hinder direct comparison. To address this challenge, we present a unified, data‐driven framework that connects atomistic interface physics with device‐level metrics using descriptor‐light machine learning. Based on high‐throughput density‐functional‐theory (DFT) calculations spanning 16 665 candidate 2D semiconductors and 80 metals, we construct a record‐scale dataset covering diverse interface chemistries and contact regimes. Trained solely on publicly available database‐derived elemental descriptors, the models predict van der Waals (vdW) barrier formation together with vertical, and lateral Schottky barrier heights (SBHs) within milliseconds, enabling rapid, ab initio‐free screening of arbitrary contacts. Validation against experimental data and quantum transport simulations confirms accurate reproduction of established contact behaviors and resistance trends. The framework further identifies over one hundred previously unexplored near‐barrier‐free interfaces and reveals physically interpretable principles governing carrier injection, establishing a scalable pathway toward intrinsically Ohmic 2D contacts.
articles.summary_en: Researchers have developed a unified, data-driven machine-learning framework using high-throughput density-functional-theory calculations to predict barrier-free metal contacts in two-dimensional semiconductors. The models rapidly forecast van der Waals barrier formation and Schottky barrier heights to enable screening of arbitrary contacts. This approach successfully identifies numerous unexplored near-barrier-free interfaces and establishes design principles for Ohmic 2D contacts.

articles.title_original: Three-dimensional hydrogel semiconductors for advanced bioelectronics
articles.title_en: Three-Dimensional Hydrogel Semiconductors for Advanced Bioelectronics
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract In this Research Highlights, we discuss a recently reported manufacturing strategy of dimensionally increased hydrogel OECT by engineering phase of double-network hydrogel and optimizing balanced electrical and ionic conductivity through porosity control. Owing to its tissue-like mechanical properties, with a Young’s modulus on the order of 10²–10³ kPa, this hydrogel semiconductor is particularly suitable for interfacing with complex three-dimensional biological tissues and is expected to mitigate inflammatory responses. Importantly, when incorporated into OECTs, the hydrogel channel maintained capacitance linearity even as the device dimensions were expanded, unlike conventional 2D film-based OECTs. Moreover, the transconductance (Gm) was substantially higher than that of stacked 2D film architectures, as the channel thickness increased. The highlighted work also demonstrated the potential of these OECTs for neuromorphic circuits that mimic biological neural networks. Future research directions would include a generalizable manufacturing strategy for 3D hydrogel OECTs that can accommodate semiconducting polymers beyond PEDOT:PSS and enable the development of not only p-type but also n-type devices.
articles.summary_en: This research highlight discusses a newly reported manufacturing strategy for dimensionally increased hydrogel organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) through phase engineering of double-network hydrogels. The hydrogel semiconductors exhibit tissue-like mechanical properties suitable for interfacing with complex biological tissues and mitigating inflammatory responses. Furthermore, these 3D hydrogel OECTs maintain capacitance linearity and show substantially higher transconductance compared to conventional 2D film architectures, opening up potential applications in neuromorphic circuits.

articles.title_original: Multistate control in 2D CuCrP2S6/Sc2CO2 multiferroic heterostructures
articles.title_en: Multistate Control in 2D CuCrP2S6/Sc2CO2 Multiferroic Heterostructures for Spintronic Devices
articles.excerpt_original: The magnetoelectric (ME) coupling effect enables effective cross-control between electric and magnetic fields, providing a crucial pathway toward next-generation low-power electronic devices. Here, we propose a two-dimensional (2D) multistate multiferroic heterostructure (MMH) composed of out-of-plane polarized CuCrP2S6 and Sc2CO2 (CCPS/SCO) to realize electric field driven multistate spintronic devices. First-principles calculations demonstrate that the CCPS/SCO heterostructure can be reversibly switched among four nonvolatile polarization states (↑↑, ↑↓, ↓↓, ↓↑) using electrical pulses, enabling simultaneous control of electronic transport, magnetic ordering, and spin orientation within a single heterostructure. By encoding the four polarization states, three distinct quantum phases are identified, i.e., out-of-plane antiferromagnetic metal, in-plane ferromagnetic semiconductor, and out-of-plane ferromagnetic metal. The microscopic mechanism underlying this strong ME coupling originates from polarization-induced interfacial charge transfer and symmetry breaking, which synergistically shift the energy level and tune the orbital occupation of Cr-d orbitals. Our proposed CCPS/SCO MMH heterostructure establishes a promising platform for high-density, low-power, and functionally reconfigurable spintronic memory.
articles.summary_en: Researchers demonstrate a two-dimensional multistate multiferroic heterostructure composed of CuCrP2S6 and Sc2CO2 that achieves reversibly switchable polarization states using electrical pulses. First-principles calculations reveal that this strong magnetoelectric coupling enables simultaneous control over electronic transport, magnetic ordering, and spin orientation. This system offers a promising pathway toward high-density, low-power, and functionally reconfigurable spintronic memory applications.

articles.title_original: Intrinsic Phonons as a Dynamic Control Knob for Catalytic Reactivity in 2D Materials
articles.title_en: Intrinsic Phonons as a Dynamic Control Knob for Catalytic Reactivity in 2D Materials
articles.excerpt_original: Catalytic activity is conventionally understood in terms of static electronic structure descriptors, with lattice vibrations treated as a passive background. Here we show that intrinsic phonon modes can serve as an active and selective control knob for catalytic reactivity in 2D materials. Using density functional theory, we demonstrate that mode-specific lattice excitations in transition metal dichalcogenides dynamically modulate their electronic structure, inducing direct-indirect bandgap transitions and substantial bandgap renormalization. In Janus WSSe, excitation of the A1 2 mode reduces the bandgap to 0.93 eV, significantly enhancing carrier transport. More importantly, these phonon-induced lattice distortions systematically tune adsorption energetics and reaction pathways. Using the oxygen evolution reaction as a model system, we find that phonon activation lowers the overpotential by up to 17%, arising from weakened adsorption of key intermediates. Crystal orbital Hamilton population and p-band center analyses reveal that this effect originates from phonon-driven modulation of orbital hybridization and bonding strength. Our results establish a dynamic, mode-selective paradigm for controlling catalytic processes via intrinsic lattice degrees of freedom, opening a route toward phonon-engineered electrocatalysis beyond static materials design.
articles.summary_en: This academic study demonstrates that intrinsic phonon modes can actively control catalytic reactivity in two-dimensional materials rather than acting as a passive background. Using density functional theory on transition metal dichalcogenides and Janus WSSe, the researchers show that mode-specific lattice excitations modulate electronic structure and improve the oxygen evolution reaction by lowering the overpotential. This research establishes a new paradigm for phonon-engineered electrocatalysis beyond traditional static materials design.

articles.title_original: Room‐temperature macroscopic observation of single‐electron quantum states
articles.title_en: Room-Temperature Observation of Single-Electron Quantum States in 2D Coplanar Architecture
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Single‐electron quantum states are confined to cryogenic observation, since miniaturization amplifies fringing capacitance that masks charge quantization. Liu et al. address this with a 2D coplanar architecture suppressing fringing capacitance, achieving a non‐volatile ~0.5 V threshold shift per electron at room temperature, an order of magnitude beyond prior devices. It bridges low‐temperature single‐electron physics and practical memory operation, stabilizing and reading out quantized electronic states under ambient conditions and extending quantum memory to room‐temperature semiconductors.
articles.summary_en: Researchers have demonstrated the macroscopic observation of single-electron quantum states at room temperature by utilizing a 2D coplanar architecture that suppresses fringing capacitance. This breakthrough achieves a non-volatile threshold shift per electron under ambient conditions, bridging low-temperature single-electron physics with practical memory operation. The development extends quantum memory and single-electron device capabilities to room-temperature semiconductor platforms.
